target: Decide PA(19,8,6), equivalently whether A_6(8,7)=19 rather than18.

primary_attestation.caption_quote: For each combinatorial design problem, the smallest open instances from the Handbook are listed, along with progress on these published elsewhere in the literature.
primary_attestation.later_source: arXiv:2505.23881v1 (29May2025), Table1(a):18,8,6 solved, not19. Parent downloaded current PDFs and confirmed both version headers and table rows.

definition: 19×8 array over{0,...,5}, each pair of columns has no repeated ordered symbol pair. Equivalently every pair of rows agrees in at most1 position (minimum Hamming distance7).
baseline: 18 known (CPro1 repository), upper19. N20 impossible: every column has at least24 equal-row pairs, so8 columns force192 distinct row pairs but C(20,2)=190. A larger code would contain20 rows.

representation: For N19 minimum coincidence count per column is21, total168 vs171 row pairs: total profile excess<=3. Balanced profile(4,3,3,3,3,3) is only one case, NOT a target restriction. Enumerate every feasible column-size profile and multiset under this budget. Run full SAT/proof logging and local search; exact-cover resolvable-packing interpretation allowed if equivalence proved.

acceptance.SAT: Explicit19×8 matrix; parent and2 independent verifiers, positive PA18 control from public CPro1data, mutations, seed replay.
acceptance.UNSAT: Complete sound encoding with justified symmetry reductions, checked UNSAT proof (e.g.LRAT) and an independent method/encoder, plus PA18 positive control. Only then combine with18 construction to prove optimum18.
acceptance.insufficient: UNSAT for balanced columns only, heuristic miss, timeout, unchecked solver assertion or unsupported textbook equivalence.
